answers.answer: Taking the title during Act makes the Exile Oathkeeper-side. At their next Wake they check victory before flipping to Usurper; if still holding the title, they flip then, and can first win at the following Wake if they remain Usurper. If they lose and later retake it, it resets to Oathkeeper, restarting the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions, ‘Usurper victory’: ‘Taking title during Act normally requires surviving to next Wake to flip, then surviving to following Wake to win. Losing and retaking title resets it to Oathkeeper.’ Wake order says Exile victory is checked before the title flip.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary requires an Exile to have a revealed true Vision, complete its goal at Wake, and have at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck. For Conquest/Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, so a tie does not qualify.
answers.evidence: The Oath table lists all four matches. Visionary victory states the universal 3-Visions-drawn requirement and says ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, no ties.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll only if Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7; otherwise continue. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll. An Exile Oathkeeper cannot permit it.
answers.evidence: ‘Stable regime’: end-of-round rolls at rounds 5/6/7, results 6 / 5–6 / 3–6; ‘An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.’

answers.answer: At round 8: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor winning alone instead of the Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifiers resolved Conquest, then Rebellion, then Sanctuary, then Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins, again with a qualified Successor replacing the Chancellor. An Exile being Oathkeeper alone does not prevent the final Empire fallback.
answers.evidence: ‘War exhaustion’ gives this exact four-step round-8 order and states the simultaneous Vision priority.

answers.answer: Supremacy Successor: hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by revealing a true Vision or becoming Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oath table lists Citizen Successor goals; Visionary victory says ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.’

answers.answer: At Wake, if holding People's Favor, either add 1 favor from your board to it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank, choosing among ties. Never remove its last favor: with one favor you must add if able; if you have none, do nothing. On the Mob side, repeat that choice once. After these steps, flip it to Mob if it has 6 or more favor. Reaching the Mob threshold at this final check does not cause a second payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake step 1 states the choices, last-favor rule, repeat on Mob side, then threshold check; it says flipping at that final step does not retroactively repeat payment.

answers.answer: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown board secrets faceup; refresh Supply; save remaining unspent Supply by moving one extra space left per unused Supply, capped at the leftmost space; then optional Rest powers once each in chosen order. Chancellor/Exile refresh according to their warbands remaining in personal bank; Citizens refresh to the exact Chancellor marker space, including the leftmost. Thus saved Supply affects next Supply through its leftward movement.
answers.evidence: ‘Rest: mandatory order’ lists all five steps, the Chancellor/Exile refresh thresholds, Citizen’s exact marker rule, and the extra leftward movement for unspent Supply.

answers.answer: Search either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. A world-deck Search costs 2 at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret changes the world-deck cost to 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw up to 3. From the world deck, drawing a Vision is announced, immediately ends that draw, and advances Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop drawing or advance the track.
answers.evidence: Search section gives both sources and costs, then distinguishes the immediate stop/track advance for a world-deck Vision from discard-pile Visions.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown on the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle. Cards from hand/advisers use the player's pawn region; a card discarded from a site in another region goes to the pile based on that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank; secrets on it go facedown to the acting player's board.
answers.evidence: ‘Discard destinations’ describes the regional cycle and remote-site card destination; attached favor returns to the bank and secrets go facedown to acting player's board.

answers.answer: There may be up to 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown; before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser. Faceup advisers cannot normally be discarded voluntarily later without a rule allowing it. Facedown cards have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card—including a Vision or site-only card—may be held facedown. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup into the separate Revealed Vision space; it is not an adviser and replaces/discards the old revealed Vision. Chancellor and Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them. A facedown adviser can be played faceup later as a minor action under Search play rules, or discarded.
answers.evidence: Search options specify the three-card adviser limit, facedown properties, and true Vision replacement; Minor actions says a facedown adviser can be played faceup as if finishing Search or discarded.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (it must have no favor or secrets), then take 2 warbands from personal bank to your board; Citizens take purple. Relics and ruins are ineligible; you need not rule the site, and a remote site you rule cannot be used. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site. Either place 1 secret to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or place 2 favor to gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank. Facedown advisers do not match; with no matches the second option gains zero secrets, though its cost is still paid. Gains are limited by finite source supply (secrets are unlimited).
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections specify costs, eligible cards, location, resource placements/gains, matching faceup advisers, and zero-secret/no-match case.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost, then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Player-held and Reliquary relics cannot be recovered. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. For People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds; put the payment on it, distribute its old favor one at a time through the suit banks starting anywhere and moving away from the world deck (wrapping), and flip it to normal if Mob. For Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds; the new holder takes 1 old secret, and the previous holder takes the rest. Recovering it from yourself returns all old secrets to you; from the shared bank, the remainder stays there. Recovering a banner has no seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Recover section specifies relic eligibility and costs, banner outbids and old-resource distribution, and that there is no seizure penalty when recovering.

answers.answer: To recover another player's Darkest Secret, their pawn's site must have a suited card that matches none of their faceup advisers. If they have no faceup advisers but there is a suited site card, it is recoverable. If they have no suited site card—an empty site or ruin-only site—it is protected. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. The protection does not apply when recovering from yourself or the shared bank.
answers.evidence: Corrected Darkest Secret protection states the suited-card condition, the no-adviser case, and that empty and ruin-only sites protect it.

answers.answer: Choose another player who rules your site or whose pawn is there; if no player rules your site, bandits may be chosen. Declare at least one target at your pawn's site, and if the defender rules that site you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics, their banners, or their pawn together with their favor. A co-located defender's relic target itself satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 give defender choice, local target requirement, mandatory target if defender rules the site, remote sites, and co-located relic/banner/pawn-and-favor targets.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Defense is shields rolled (each double-symbol doubles shields, multipliers stack), plus defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's own force warbands. Count full swords, and each pair of hollow swords adds 1 (a leftover hollow sword adds nothing). The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. The attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower means defender wins.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2, 4, and 5 state die selection, defense formula, skulls, sword scoring, exact-enough sacrifices, and strict-win/tie rule.

answers.answer: After the roll, the defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to its board; bandits cannot be killed and hide. If the attacker wins, they may place any number—including zero—of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; zero leaves the site to bandits unless another power applies. They take all targeted relics and banners. A banner seized by Campaign (or otherwise taken outside Recover) loses 2 resources down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site without Supply, and separately may burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Site travel restrictions such as Shrouded Wood still apply.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–7 give defeat losses, zero garrison option, all targets taken, banner seizure penalty, and the separate travel/board-favor effects with site restrictions.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Defender and Allies activate their relevant Campaign modifiers; the title's defense bonus is shared by the defending side, and allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not another player's advisers; a player pays for their own plan and the same plan cannot be shared. The specified temporary non-Imperial cases are: a Citizen attacking the Chancellor or another Citizen, or the Chancellor attacking a Citizen. In an intra-Empire Campaign, only the specified attacker/defender loses Imperial status for that Campaign, not every Citizen.
answers.evidence: Campaign step 1 and ‘Imperial defense’ describe temporary status, Chancellor's automatic alliance, other allies, shared title bonus, warband and plan conditions.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs by origin/destination region are: from Cradle, 1 to Cradle, 2 to Provinces, 4 to Hinterland; from Provinces, 2 to each region; from Hinterland, 4 to Cradle, 2 to Provinces, 3 to Hinterland. The destination may be any different site, not just an adjacent one. A facedown destination is revealed and gets its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number Travel costs first, then other increases/decreases. A modifier saying ‘spend no Supply’ overrides all cost increases; site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by name or power.
answers.evidence: Travel section contains the full cost table, reveal/setup rule, and modifier order including the no-Supply override.

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, or exile another Citizen; the Scepter's powers cannot be used on the turn it was taken. A Citizenship offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic, and may negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics; the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. On acceptance, flip to Citizen, replace all own warbands on board/map with purple (choosing removals if purple is insufficient), discard a revealed Vision, flip Usurper to Oathkeeper, end the recipient's Act if it is their turn, and refresh to full Supply. Exchange the promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced-Citizenship powers bypass negotiation. Separately, a Citizen without the Scepter may self-exile by giving the Scepter holder favor equal to own board warbands plus their secrets on board and on denizen/relic/edifice cards; they cannot do this while holding the Scepter, and it ends their Act. Exiling another Citizen has a specified favor payment, makes them Exile and replaces their board purple warbands; map garrisons remain purple.
answers.evidence: ‘Citizenship and exile during play’ covers offer, acceptance, self-exile, and exiling a Citizen, including the exact offer promise and exchanges.

answers.answer: A victory by Vision alone sets the next Oath to match that Vision. Any other victory, including multiple victory methods, allows any Oath except the current one. If the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards—including boxed boards—to Exile; the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped, with normal offer cost/relic rules ignored, but cannot offer themself Chronicle Citizenship. For rebuilding the world deck, shuffle remaining in-play denizens; put 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards total) on top, then 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), with remaining denizens below. The Chronicle aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect; that would make a 14-card top stack, so it is 10 denizens + 2 Visions.
answers.evidence: Chronicle steps 1–2 state Oath choice and board turnover; step 9 specifies top stack ‘10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12’ and explicitly rejects the aid's ‘12 denizens + 2.’
